history.text: He came from the Caribbean. A merchant's ledgers taught him to reckon; storms at sea taught him that a life could be rewritten overnight.
He put what he had seen into words. People read them and began to believe this young man deserved the chance to continue his education.
In 1781, French and American forces surrounded Yorktown. Years of marches, dispatches, and disputes brought Hamilton to the foot of a British redoubt.
In 1781, French and American forces surrounded Yorktown. Years of marches and dispatches brought Hamilton to the foot of a British redoubt.
Hamilton's troops took Redoubt No. 10, while French forces took the neighboring Redoubt No. 9. The siege tightened.
Days later, British forces surrendered at Yorktown. Victory belonged to many people fighting together. The war had not formally ended, but its course had changed.
On the back of the letter, a name has been written several times. The ink varies in darkness; the final attempt is especially clear.
A draft lies on an empty table. Its final line stops halfway: if our voices deserve to be heard...
